memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'No one is to come with you or be seen anywhere on the mountain; not even the flocks and herds may graze in front of the mountain.' So Moses chiselled out two stone tablets like the first ones and went up Mount Sinai early in the morning, as the Lord had commanded him; and he carried the two stone tablets in his hands." - Exod 34:3-4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
No crowds. No assistants. Not even a stray animal grazing nearby. Moses goes up alone.

There are meetings with God that cannot happen in company. We need the gathered church, and Scripture never permits us to neglect it (Heb 10:25). But there are also things God does in us only when the room is empty and nobody is watching.

Jesus modelled this deliberately. He often withdrew to lonely places to pray (Luke 5:16), rising very early while it was still dark (Mark 1:35). If the Son of God guarded solitude with the Father, how much more do we need it.

Notice too the obedience in the details. God said morning; Moses went early in the morning. God said two tablets; Moses carried two tablets in his hands. There is nothing dramatic here — just a man doing exactly what he was told, on time, carrying what he was asked to carry.

Much of the Christian life looks like this. Not mountaintop drama, but quiet, unglamorous obedience done carefully.

In a world of constant noise and notifications, solitude with God has become genuinely difficult. It will not happen by accident. You will have to chisel out the time the way Moses chiselled the stone.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. When did you last spend unhurried time alone with God?
2. What would you need to change to make solitude with God possible?
3. Is there a small, unglamorous act of obedience God is asking of you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, help me carve out time to be alone with You. Teach me to obey You in the small details. Amen.
